speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the mechanism of the rear-end collision, specifically if your leg was extended when the dashboard hit it? I also need to know if you have any numbness or tingling in your right leg or foot.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you able to bear any weight on your right leg, and does moving your right hip in any direction significantly worsen the groin pain? I need to assess the stability of the hip joint and rule out a fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The specific positioning of your right leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is a classic sign of a posterior hip dislocation. I am going to confirm this immediately by ordering imaging. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray
